classifications.rationale: The President immediately establishes and structures an internal advisory conference; this is executive organization, not a change to private legal rights.
classifications.evidence: There is hereby established a conference to be known as the Administrative Conference of the United States

classifications.rationale: The President assigns the selection of a chair and defines the Conference’s advisory purpose; these are internal organizational actions with no substantive legal consequence for private parties.
classifications.evidence: one of whom he shall designate to be Chairman of the Conference

classifications.rationale: The Conference is mandatorily assigned to study agency procedures; any legal consequence could arise only from later, separate action based on its work.
classifications.evidence: the Conference shall conduct studies of the efflciency, adequacy and fairness of procedures

classifications.rationale: The Conference and designated officials must report, structure membership, and appoint members; these are internal reporting and staffing functions that take effect administratively without changing private legal rights.
classifications.evidence: The composition of the general membership of the Conference shall be determined by the Council

classifications.rationale: The Attorney General, Conference, Chairman, and Council receive mandatory or discretionary staffing and internal-governance duties; these organize Conference operations rather than dictate a later legal outcome affecting private parties.
classifications.evidence: The Attorney General of the United States is hereby authorized and directed to furnish to the Conference research and staff assistance

classifications.rationale: The Council is authorized to manage membership, meetings, congressional participation, and proposed internal rules; these are ongoing administrative functions with no independently prescribed legal consequence.
classifications.evidence: The Council is hereby authorized to perform the following functions

classifications.rationale: The Council is authorized to set study proposals, consider reports, and transmit recommendations to the President; these are advisory and reporting functions whose outputs do not themselves alter legal rights.
classifications.evidence: to transmit them to the President together with the views of the Council

classifications.rationale: Executive agencies must provide cooperation, information, assistance, and potentially staff details to support the Conference; these are internal resource and coordination requirements, not prescribed legal outcomes for regulated parties.
classifications.evidence: All executive departments and administrative agencies of the Federal Government are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Conference
